HUNTPRO Eagle Pattern Stainless Steel Slingshot Metal Hunting Slingshot Kit, High Velocity Catapult Sling Shot with 3 Flat Rubber Bands & Steel Ammo Balls Kit for Adults Shooting Indoor Outdoor At first glance this was a nice looking slingshot that I was eager to get assembled and try out. Everything you need to assemble this item is included in one handy little case. Extra screws, Allen wrench, 2 extra rubber bands, and steel ammo. Because of how this is constructed, it took me a little longer to get the bands connected and secured, but once it was done it looked good and was ready. Or so I thought. As I started holding it more and aiming it, I felt something protruding from the handle and looking closely saw it was the eagle design and the bottom tail of the eagle was sticking out a little when it should have been level with the slingshot surface. I tried to fix this by hammering the slingshot protected with a towel, only to find the entire eagle design moves every time I tried to use the slingshot. That metal protrusion is really a safety issue.

I then went ahead and wore gloves to try out the slingshot. The bands are really nice and stretchy and the stainless ammo balls were perfect for practice. The slingshot shoots pretty well and is comfortable to hold. Even though the handle is kind of short, the large metal loop makes it easier to hold because it conforms better to my hand. I do like this slingshot, but feel something needs to be done about the eagle design and how it moves such that the sharp edges stick out.
text_fidelity_b: HUNTPRO Eagle Pattern Stainless Steel Slingshot Metal Hunting Slingshot Kit, High Velocity Catapult Sling Shot with 3 Flat Rubber Bands & Steel Ammo Balls Kit for Adults Shooting Indoor Outdoor

Dynacraft Childrens-Bicycles Tony Hawk I bought a set of bikes for my family for Christmas. I got my wife a nice beach cruiser, my middle-school daughter a nice mountain bike with a rack so she can ride to school with her clarinet, my son a cheapie bike for a 6 year old to learn on, and myself a lower-end BMX to ride around the neighborhood with the family. Always had a love of the BMX style bike, and although I knew the one I got was a cheaper model, having Tony Hawk’s name on it was reassuring, and it had good reviews.

After 4 months of street/easy trail riding (that my 6 year old can do - not extreme or punishing on a bike), the right pedal arm fell off of the crank. It clamps down on a hex shaft, using a hex head bolt to tighten it, but as much as I could tighten the bolt it will not stay on. The crank assembly is also coming loose, and needs constant fighting in between reattachments of the right pedal.

This bike is going on the curb shortly, and I’ll be in the market for a higher quality BMX bike.

Could have been a fluke on this one. Maybe the tolerances from manufacturing were out of standard - whatever - but if you can toss in another hundred or two I would look for a higher quality bike.
text_fidelity_b: Dynacraft Childrens-Bicycles Tony Hawk

text_fidelity_a:
HOMGIM Exercise Bike [[VIDEOID:bf4a381ea2346e023f15723581aa57ec]] This bike is easy to set up and adjust, and it has lots of features that make it a useful addition to my fitness program. I've uploaded a short video showing the adjustments and features, but I'll run thru them quickly here, too. Let me know if you find anything here useful.

You'll want to set the seat height so that your thigh) (hip to knee) is parallel to the ground at the top of the rotation. Then slide the seat back to where it's an easy reach forward to the handlebars without holding a lot of your weight there.

The tension on the pedals is adjusted by a big black knob just below the handlebars. There are also separate tensioned handles that you can pull to get an upper body (arms, shoulders, back, and abs) workout as you ride.

You can scroll through various screens on the electronic display. The best of these, in my opinion, is a heart rate monitor that reads your pulse while your hands are on the handlebar sensors. You can also get distance, time, and speed traveled. Its really a pretty capable machine, considering the low price.

This little bike folds up when not in use, so you can store it in a closet, lay it on the floor along a wall, or lean it in a corner. It isn't as beefy (or likely as durable) as one of the fancy spinning bikes at the gym, but this one is a lot more affordable, and meets my needs at home just fine. Check out the video, and let me know this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: HOMGIM Exercise Bike

text_fidelity_a: Golf Rangefinder with Slope, 1093Y Red Display Laser Range Finder with High-Precision Flag Pole Locking Vibration, 6X Magnification, Slope Mode, Magnetic Mount, Type-C Recharging I do have a chain link fence around the front of my house while the back area is open (without fencing).  My area is abutted by Army Corp of Engineer "wild" land that goes (about a quarter of a mile) to a large lake not far from my house.  Just this past week my neighbor and I spotted a bobcat in the wild land back there!  We have coyotes, wild boars, raccoons, opossums, armadillos and a few other critters we've seen and documented.  This laser range finder has allowed me to get an idea of how close some of the wild life is getting to my yard.  I have small dogs and the coyotes worry me more than most of the other critters.  So when I spot one slinking around the edge of the woods, I grab this range finder and document when, where and how far they were from me.  At some point, if they get to be a bit too bold, the neighbors and I will have to report the pack as being dangerous.  Having documented the times, the places and how far they were from me, a human, will be helpful in proving that they need to be trapped and moved or dealt with in some other way.  I know this range finder is good for golf or even hunting - I guess my use is more akin to hunting, but I will say that it is easy to use, sighting in on the critter to find the distance.  That's what I need to know!
text_fidelity_b: Golf Rangefinder with Slope, 1093Y Red Display Laser Range Finder with High-Precision Flag Pole Locking Vibration, 6X Magnification, Slope Mode, Magnetic Mount, Type-C Recharging

The belt helped a little with increasing weight, by giving a solid surface to push your gut into. I use it on my heavy sets now for squat and deadlift and it works fine.

The belt has a good thickness and width. I have a 33" waist and use the fourth from the last set of holes. My fiancee is able to use the same belt (she wears size 0 womens) albeit on the tightest set of holes. It'll take a week or so to loosen up and will continue to for awhile. After a month or so of regular use my belt is still a little starchy.

My complaint is the double latch. It's difficult to latch and unlatch. Don't be that guy walking around in a belt the whole time you're at the gym--the belt is really only that useful for heavy lifts. I resorted to just buckling the top one instead of wrestling with it after each set.

text_fidelity_a:
DeskCycle Ellipse Under Desk Elliptical Machine - Get Fit While You Work with Our Compact Mini Seated Elliptical Machine - Burn Calories, Boost Energy, Tone Muscles, and Increase Productivity I ordered this item because I wanted something I could take to work for under my desk so I could get some exercise while working. I have a sit-down job and need to move my legs sometimes throughout the day. The listing for this ellipse made it sound very appealing so I decided to give a try, and I am happy to report I am thrilled with this item! It has so many great things about it.

First, it was easy to assemble. It was just a matter of putting a couple screws into the bottom of each pedal to attach them, inserting the batteries into the digital readout, then hooking the wire from the base unit into the readout. The screws and batteries were provided with the unit. Very simple and it was ready to go after that. The digital readout turns on automatically when you start pedaling, and shuts itself off a few minutes after you have finished pedaling. To reset the digital reading back to zero before it shuts down is just a matter of pressing the white button for a few seconds and the readings will zero out. While you are using this desk cycle, it will keep track of how many rotations/steps were taken. You can also view RPM, time, and calories. This unit has a tension adjustment knob that is also very simple, just turn to a higher number and the pedaling gets much harder. Or you can keep it at the lowest setting to make the pedaling easy. The pedals are huge, so should work for any size foot whether or not you are wearing shoes. Also, this unit is ultra quiet. You could certainly use this in a room where someone is sleeping and not wake them up.

As you can see in my photos, there is a sticker on the top of the unit. This sticker does not really go there, there was one of these on each of the pedals as a warning that you should never stand on the pedals. The reason I kept one of the stickers and affixed it to the top of the unit is in case someone else decides to try it out in my office when I am not around. I can see where the temptation to want to try to “walk” on the pedals would be very tempting.

If I had to say anything negative about this unit would only be that it is very heavy. But it has to be in order to be able to stay in place while you are using it. It’s just that the weight doesn’t leave it very portable such that you could just move it from room to room all the time. Having said that, I appreciate the heavy weight in that it is part of what makes it the superb quality that it is, and the weight will prevent it from sliding on the floor while using it.
5 stars for this fantastic piece of equipment!
text_fidelity_b: DeskCycle Ellipse Under Desk Elliptical Machine - Get Fit While You Work with Our Compact Mini Seated Elliptical Machine - Burn Calories, Boost Energy, Tone Muscles, and Increase Productivity

text_fidelity_a: Rapidfire Chimney Starter I'm very upset at the quality of this item I just purchased brand new.  I just used it yesterday for the first time along with my new Weber grill, filled it with plain charcoal only to where the top hole is on the top (we counted 50 briquettes), and THIS is what my brand new charcoal starter now looks like!  SEE THE PICTURES I JUST TOOK, 2 from the outside (left and right sides) and two from the inside (left and right). After the first 10 minutes, I saw that the charcoal on the top was still completely black with no signs of the flame touching them.  Just then, I saw a very strange chemical-type reaction occurring on the outside of the canister!  It was as if a magic invisible paintbrush with white paint on it was stroking heavy stripes of paint around the outside of it!  We were shocked to see this odd thing happening!  About 15 minutes later, We finally saw small flames inside that were approaching the top briquettes.  As soon as we saw the top ones beginning to get a little grey color, we emptied it out, and the whole process took 30 minutes -- not the 15-20 we were expecting.  After we poured in the briquettes, which were already fully completely white and falling apart at the bottom, we began to cook with what remained in the canister.  I don't think this thing was operating properly at all, and I knew something was wrong when I saw this horrible discoloration happening only 10 minutes into the process.  I feel like this was made with some cheap foreign material and am very upset that my new chimney starter was ruined and unable to perform on DAY ONE.  I don't even think this thing is safe, because if it's being compromised in this way and the metal is underperforming, who knows what's going to happen to the metal on SUBSEQUENT uses, the metal and the bolts that is supposedly holding the handle onto the canister??  Is this now going to melt and break off just as we're holding onto it and unloading it into the grill??
text_fidelity_b: Rapidfire Chimney Starter

Bracelet making requires a lighter to singe ends so parents beware that you may need to help younger children and even older children may get burnt from hot paracord that was just burnt. I am going to buy a block kit to make these I think,  it might help their like thirteen bucks  and have measurements built right on it. text_fidelity_a:
Pro-Series 63134 Q-Slot 2 Black 2-Bike Hitch Mounted Bike Carrier As others have already pointed out, this rack has a tendency to loosen up and potentially lose bikes. The reason this happens is because the main vertical tube is loose (has some free-play in the lower holes and rocks forward and back). Every time the bikes rock forward/back, the restraints move slightly up, no matter how tightly you screwed them down. There are several solutions (which can be combined for added safety):

1) Throw a tie-down strap over the bikes, attaching the hooks to the bottom bracket. This will keep the bikes from falling, and even moving at all if the strap is tight enough.

2) Prevent the free play in the top tube. The way I did this was as follows:
- Overdrill the hitch pin hole to 5/16" or even 3/8". The small 1/4" hitch pin loosens the hole over time, resulting in wobble. Use a 5/16" (or bigger) hitch pin, available at big hardware stores or amazon.
- Reinforce the holes in the tube. I did this by epoxying in a 5/16" coupling nut cut to length, then drilling it out so that the bolt/pin fit tightly.
- Reinforce the holes in the frame. I did this by epoxying on tight-fitting washers (1/4" washers I drilled to 5/16").

text_fidelity_a:
Firmstrong Bruiser Man Single Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle This bike has turned out to be a very good purchase for me.

I live on my boat in Los Angles and am able to attend to 90% of my brick and mortar shopping without using my car since this bike is beefy and has no problem handling a couple of saddle bag type baskets as well as a basket on the handlebars. A 36 pack of canned beer rides securely on the rear rack held in place with bungee cords

I bought the three speed model and am glad I did. Even though the area around us is pretty flat there are a few sloped ramps, on our great local bike paths, that make me appreciate the ability to shift down. Down wind on a level surface, or down hill, the high gear is useful. Some days the breeze off the ocean is strong enough to cause me to shift down when headed up wind. The three speed has no derailleur so the bike has a chain guard.

This bike is very easy to ride and takes a lot of the back and hand stress out of riding my bike. Im 72 and outgrew dropped handlebars about half a century ago.

It took me a few days to get used to coaster brakes again, after decades of cool bikes with hand brakes. But now Im cool with the coaster brake and really like the lack of clutter on the handle bars.

I added a bell, lights and a holder for my smart phone. I also added a really nice rear view mirror which is a great safety feature. I got a nice beefy lock on Amazon and really like the fact that I can drop it in my basket instead of going to the trouble of installing it on the mount on the bike every time I take off.

Since I live in southern California fenders seemed pointless so I skipped that accessory.

The bike is easy to ride with its big tires but is not fast. If you want a fast bike a beach cruiser is probably not what you should buy.

Unless I have some compelling reason to get in my car I do all my local travel on my bike. Its easier, faster many times, and there are no parking hassles or cost. I rode it 25 miles round trip to a doctor appointment a week ago. It was along the beach where there is a nice bike path and lots of scenery. It was not an exhausting experience but then I was not in a big hurry.

As I ride to the gym every morning Im passed by cyclists on high tech bikes who are bent into incredibly uncomfortable looking positions over their dropped handle bars. As they zoom past I reflect on the fact that I definitely bought the right bike for me and also that some people should not be wearing lycra cycling outfits.

The only negative about this purchase was that the packaging on the bike was not adequate to protect it in shipment. The three speed shifter on the rear axel had broken through the cardboard box and got scratched up in shipment. The damage did not look like it was more than cosmetic and I did not want o hassle with repacking the bike to return it so I went ahead and accepted as it was.
text_fidelity_b: Firmstrong Bruiser Man Single Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Full-Size Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor A good heart rate monitor and watch for people into fitness but are not super serious athletes. You can also wear this watch as a nice, functional regular watch too.

The operation of this watch is similar to the basic Timex ironman watches with some additional features (it's necessary to read the manual to understand all the features).

Pros: Watch is very comfortable - it's big but it stays in place. The strap is very adjustable and should fit nearly every wrist. The heart rate strap is also comfortable. The large face is a bonus because it's that much easier to glance down and see the numbers when you're running.
Lots of features - Chrono counts time and records your total workout length or laps, and gives an average HR for each lap. The interval timer counts down and can do timed intervals (eg. run for 8 min, walk 30 seconds). The review feature will give you average HR, max/min HR for the workout, how many minutes you spent in your "target" HR and calories burnt, which is nice to see if you want to judge how intense your workout was. It also gives the average HR for each of your laps.

It has an alarm clock and a really good Indiglo setting for the dark.

Very easy to use the HR monitor, basically put it on and press the HR button on the watch and it automatically starts getting HR data.

Cons: The review feature doesn't give the time spent in each HR zone over the whole workout, only your target HR zone. This seems like a big oversight because it's as important to see how much time you spend in the high HR "red" zones as well as the lower zones. This means that if you're running up and down varied terrain, you have to look down at your wrist to see what your HR is and remember what zone that is for you and guess how much time you've spent in each zone.

If you're only using one of the interval timers, you have to set the second interval timer to 0, which is very annoying. It would be easy to have a feature asking if you want to use one or two timers.

It doesn't store more than 1 workout review in the watch, so you have to write the info down if you want a record of your workouts. This is ridiculous for a watch at this price point.

It's not ANT+ compatible, so there's no way to increase the functionality like tying it to a GPS device. I suppose they want you to buy the next level up if you want to record that type of fitness data.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Full-Size Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
QOGIR Resistance Trainer for Disc Golf, Practice Backhand or Forehand Throws to Improve Your Disc Golf Technique, Increase Strength in Your Pull Through, Gain Extra Distance, Disc Shaped Grip. A little background: I'm a righty, but due to disc-elbow problems (tennis elbow for disc golfers) I'm training my left arm to throw. The control issues are coming around, however so far I'm only getting about half the distance. When I started with the right arm years ago I noticed growth in the muscle over time as my distance improved. Hence my interest in this training device for the left arm. I want to quickly get back to the same success with the left arm.

I hooked this up to a couple of wall studs in my partially finished basement. After using it several times I can tell it's giving the arm a workout. I tried all three band combinations and can definitely tell the difference.

One concern is that the tension on the disc requires a very firm grip. Fortunately the device comes with a safety strap to keep the disc attached to your arm should your grip slip. My concern is that it might teach me to grip more firmly than needed on the course. I think I can adjust for that, so it may be a non-concern.

If you don't have something firm to attach to like a tree or a wall stud, the kit includes a piece to put into a door frame. A word of caution is to only use this from the side of the door where you would be pulling the door shut. You definitely don't want the door to open while you have the disc pulled back in full tension and have that door piece come flying at you.

My only complaint is that I found no instructions. It is possible that I overlooked them in the box and tossed them out. I was able to find what I needed in the Amazon description.

I'm betting that the next few weeks will see an improvement in my lefty distance!
text_fidelity_b: QOGIR Resistance Trainer for Disc Golf, Practice Backhand or Forehand Throws to Improve Your Disc Golf Technique, Increase Strength in Your Pull Through, Gain Extra Distance, Disc Shaped Grip.

text_fidelity_a:
Wurkkos DL30 Scuba Diving Flashlight - Scuba Dive Light Super Bright Max 3600 Lumen with 5000K 90CRI,100m Underwater Flashlight IPX-8 Waterproof Submersible Flashlight with USB Charger This flashlight is a bit heavier than others in this size range. I think that is leaning more toward the battery size. The 21700 battery weighs 2.5 ounces whereas the 18650 is 1.5 ounces. The flashlight without the 21700 battery weighs 4.9 ounces. Another thing is it gets very warm from holding it in your hand on high mode for 5 minutes. A few minutes longer and it gets HOT and almost hard to hold unless you are wearing gloves. With this said the flashlight is designed for diving and stays a lot cooler under water. I submerged it in cool water and the flashlight does not get more than warm on high mode. It is the 3 LEDs that cause all the heat.

I love the brightness and the ease of turning the switch on and off. The 3 brightness settings are a good feature in my opinion and work flawlessly. To show how bright the high setting is, I included a picture of our stove with kitchen light off and standing about 7 feet back and no camera flash. If you store the flashlight for long periods of time, or if traveling and want to make sure the flashlight doesn't accidently turn on, you can just turn the tail cap backwards less than 1 turn and the flashlight is totally off. It works, I tested it! Wonderful!! The lens is very solid and thick. It appears to be nearly indestructible. Another feature is this item comes with a cover adapter for using the smaller 18650 battery that is standard in most flashlights. The 18650 wouldn't have as long a running time but runs a little cooler using this flashlight above water. We tested a fully charged 18650 on high for 5 minutes and it drained the battery to 64 percent. It is also just a bit less bright but noticeable. Testing the 21700 battery fully charged for 5 minutes above water drained the battery to 87 percent and when putting it back to charge it finished to 100 percent in about 17 minutes. We used a MiBoxer 8 battery charger that shows percentages while charging. Amazon sells them and we love it.

This flashlight in my opinion really is best underwater use. I also think if it was used as a normal flashlight and running it for 15 minutes or more on high on a hot evening could burn out the LEDs from the heat. The manual does not mention this and it says the flashlight has a built in ATR (advanced temperature regulation) and will reduce the power under certain situations of excessive heat to prevent overheating.

If you just wanted to use it above water for shorter times to find something lost like your wife's wedding ring because she got mad at you, this little gem is excellent and fits into most any size pocket. But it is SO bright you really do NOT want to look into it, and also have to be careful not to shine it in anyone’s face, and that includes pets.

Overall this is a great flashlight and I recommend it for quality and value!
text_fidelity_b: Wurkkos DL30 Scuba Diving Flashlight - Scuba Dive Light Super Bright Max 3600 Lumen with 5000K 90CRI,100m Underwater Flashlight IPX-8 Waterproof Submersible Flashlight with USB Charger

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos Let's say that you are confronted by an attacker who demands something of value from you. You whip out your "police strength" red pepper get and hit him full in the face even though he is still eight feet away. After a second or two, he begins to laugh and keeps coming at you. What went wrong? The spray deployed exactly as you tested it, yet this guy seemed immune. It was made by a reputable company. And all the reviews you read were extremely positive. But what no one bothered to do was to test the formula on themselves.

Test this on myself? What kind of stupidity is this? Think of it this way. Would you buy a gun and depend on it to defend yourself and/or your family without testing it previously? Of course not. The problem here is that it's easy to test guns, knives, clubs and other weapons by hitting something with it and assessing the damage. No one gets hurt and yet you can become very comfortable by mastering the proper delivery and seeing the expected results. But pepper spray is another matter entirely. No one in their right mind wants to spray themselves in the face. Certainly not the first 21 reviewers of this product. They all seemed to be perfectly happy that the spray deployed as advertised. No offense to any of them but some of you might end up trusting your lives to this product.

But it's really pretty easy to test on yourself. I was a product development manager for a small defense corporation about 40 years ago. I had to vouch for any product that we developed and sold. Putting a defective product in the hands of someone who truly needed it (even back then) would result in a substantial lawsuit. One of the items we developed and eventually sold was one of the first self defense sprays available to the average consumer. We would pay volunteers to take a full shot in the face as we developed and improved the formula. When we began production there was always the problem of if the canisters were filled with the proper formula. Since I was unwilling to shoot myself in the face while randomly sampling dozens of these units, I would test out the sprayer on the back of my hand.

If you want to truly rely on this product, here is what you need to do. Find a sheltered (from the wind) outdoor area away from people and animals. Your back should be toward any (even) minor breeze. Hold your left hand out from your body, unfasten the safety trigger, and shoot a small stream onto the back of your hand. Hold your breath while doing so and then step away from any residual mist. Your hand should have a large orange spot on it and you should immediately feel a strong tingling or burning sensation on the back of your hand. There were no instructions that I could find that told you to shake the canister first -- so I didn't.

Unfortunately nothing happened! No stinging or burning. Even though I was just recovering from a bad cold, I put my nose within an inch of the formula and took a quick sniff. Nothing! I tried the whole exercise again after this time shaking the canister first. The results? A more consistent mixture on the back of my hand, but again no deterrent that I could detect. With my damaged and tender nose and still sore throat, i would have been expecting discomfort of an epic nature. So my guess is that this particular canister was faulty. On the other hand, no other reviewer has tested this on themselves to corroborate my findings. Perhaps the company will contact me to try and figure out why it doesn't work. This isn't my first rodeo, but it is my only shot at life. If this product failed me at the only time I really needed it, I wouldn't be around to ask for a refund.

NOTE: There was a direct sale company (We Care America) back in the late 1970's that also sold a personal defense spray. 60 Minutes (or some other news program) proved on a televised segment that the spray didn't work as advertised, taking what was once a viable company into bankruptcy. Thousands of those canisters were sold to people who believed that they were going to be adequately protected by WCA's product. That's when I knew that I had to test these things for myself.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos

Cons:

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I wanted this specifically for its heart rate monitor and sleep monitor--something I can basically wear all the time. I specifically did not want a watch, because I wear a watch on my other arm. So this is just right for that. It's a tad bigger than it ideally could be. I hope future generations will slim down and maybe be more flexible and/or add more interesting sensors.

The sleep monitor seems to work okay. I previously had a Microsoft Band 2, and I feel it may have been better at that.

Since I don't use it as a watch, I like the option to turn off the feature to show time when lifting it up. So it stays black unless I really want it to show me something.

It lets you set like 7 alarms, which can repeat, and I use them to remind myself to drink water. So that's a nice plus.

It does seem a little slow to sync. Specifically, I often want to set a silent alarm right before bed, and it takes like a minute to sync. Then I set the alarm, and it takes several seconds to sync that. Then I can finally turn it on, and wait a few seconds to sync that. Pretty cumbersome. The Microsoft Band let you set it quickly on the Band, so it's much better in that way. (But my Band broke during normal use, and I went through a LOT of trouble to get Microsoft to replace it. A lot. Very bad customer service, so I can't recommend it.)

The battery life is good on this, but it's not great. That said, it's much easier to charge than the Blaze, which I also tried. I basically just charge it while I'm in the shower (a trick I learned for the Band), and that's more than enough. I have to say, I have almost gotten in the shower with it a few times. It is easy to forget you have it on!

So I think it's probably the best continuous HR and sleep monitor option that is specifically not trying to pretend to double as a smart watch.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity You could assemble the components for a better bike hoisting system at any decent hardware store, but the part you would buy would cost two or three times as much, and you would spend a fair amount of time figuring out what to buy and how to assemble it.

I see several review that report the packaging indicates a lesser weight capacity than the 100 lb indicated in the listing. My packaging shows the weight capacity as 45 kg -- 100 lb. Regardless, I am confident that, in fact, much more than 100 lb. could be supported by this hardware. The actual limiting factor on weight capacity will not be the hardware provided, but rather the installation method. The box includes screws with plastic anchors that are normally used for installing screws in sheetrock. Anyone who uses those to attach to a sheetrock ceiling will almost certainly have a problem. Even if the plastic anchors are used to attach the hardware to wood trusses the result will be weaker than if screwed directly into the wood after a proper size hole has been pre-drilled. Other reviews contain suggestions for mounting. The instructions provided fail to provide guidance on the need for a secure mounting.

It is easy to overlook on the installation instructions the correct routing of the rope used for lifting. There is a hole in the cam lock fitting through which the cord should be threaded. Unfortunately the hole is barely large enough for the provided rope, which would make it difficult to upsize the rope.

Which brings me to the issue of the gaps between pulley cheeks and the sheaves. The gap is enough that the provided rope can jump out of the sheave groove and become wedged. The sheaves are designed so that squeezing the cheeks to reduce the gap results in friction at the axle before the gap is significantly reduced. While a larger rope could eliminate the risk of jamming, the hole in the cam lock does not permit such a substitution. It is for this reason, and the potential that a person could be misled by the plastic sheetrock anchors and fail to attach to solid wood, that I am giving 4 stars rather than 5.

Additional comments -- As others mention, the hooks to hang the bike do not really have enough curve to hold securely and you probably will need to do some bending to get a good result. My seat does not have a structure to which the hooks would attach, so I use a cord under a frame section and secure the hooks to that. If you have a speedometer or the like mounted on handle bars there is a possibility of conflict with hooks, and you may need to be careful to avoid damage to any wire connecting to a sensor. The cleat provided to tie off the rope when the bike is lifted is definitely pretty cheesy, but the cam lock is good enough that the cleat is really not needed. If you are a belt and suspenders person you might want to upgrade the cleat. Otherwise the cleat basically just provides a method to get excess rope out of the way.

So while this is not perfect, it provides a good solution at a good price, and I would buy another one if I had a second bike.
text_fidelity_b: Bike Hoist Bicycle Lift for Garage Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Mountain Bicycle Hanging Rack with 3 Pulley and 45 ft Adjustable Rope | 100 lb Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
FEND One Foldable Bike Helmet - Adult Mens and Womens Bike Helmet - Collapsible by 50% of Original Size - Safety Certified for Bicycle Road Bike Scooter Cycling Commuter Helmet… I've never been a regular wearer of helmets so I can't compare this to other brands, but this one suits me. The medium/large fits me well, and it's comfortable to wear throughout longer rides. It's also cooler than I expected, which is a real benefit as I live in a hot and often humid climate. And though it shouldn't matter, I like the simple design of this helmet as opposed to those that have a more aerodynamic look, so to speak. And I really appreciate the low-key logo; it's tasteful, not garish like you see on so many products.

But the most important thing for me is the fold. The main thing keeping me from wearing a helmet before was having to lump around a bowl. I know that's a bad reason, but it's the truth. This folds down enough to easily fit into all of my bike bags and even the small backpack that I often carry as a purse. Admittedly, it's a squeeze for the latter, and I don't carry much in that purse anyway, but the fact that it fits means that I'll use it, and using it is definitely safer than going without.

I was lucky to get a nice discount on this (for Prime Day, I think, though perhaps it was some other deal), but I think it's worth it at its regular price. Of course I hope never to give this the ultimate test, but it feels like a sound helmet and works for the way I bike. I'd definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: FEND One Foldable Bike Helmet - Adult Mens and Womens Bike Helmet - Collapsible by 50% of Original Size - Safety Certified for Bicycle Road Bike Scooter Cycling Commuter Helmet…

text_fidelity_a:
Gun Sight Compatible with Salt&Gun 3.0 2.5 2.0 with Manual and Constant Lighting Modes (Gun not Included) This laser comes with six batteries and you only need three so you have one set for backup. The laser itself in my opinion works good and is bright with a thin beam. You can adjust the beam with the included tool. The attached button cord also works good. I could turn it on and off easily and it always worked properly. Mounting the laser was also a non-issue and tightened good.

The problem with this laser is the button switch located on the back cover of the laser. I had a horrible time getting it to work properly. After studying this thing for awhile, I discovered after removing the battery cover that the spring was crooked and would move the batteries out of position. The result was that the spring tension and spring not making center contact was causing the laser to not work properly. The spring was loose and wobbly too. I tried bending it to center but it only made it worse. My husband had spare various size springs in his shop so was able to remake one that fit better. After about an hour of work we finally got it fixed. I had to make sure the spring was dead center when closing the cap so the batteries wouldn't move out of place and had enough tension so when pressing the on/off button it would work. Another little issue is the batteries do not fit perfect inside the case and are a bit wobbly. So there is that.

I hope you have better luck and maybe this was a glitch in the one I received. I really believe the switch could have been designed better. After all, you want the laser to work when you need it. I cannot in all honesty give this item more than 3 stars and I would not recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Gun Sight Compatible with Salt&Gun 3.0 2.5 2.0 with Manual and Constant Lighting Modes (Gun not Included)

Plastimo Iris 50 Bearing and Orientation Compasss Functional, water-resistant, floats, accurate, relatively stable, protective housing, luminescent and fair price.

Use as a bearing compass and backup heading compass.

Allows reading a bearing while being gently pitched, rolled. Scale is in 1* increments. Under flat conditions easy to read down to the 1*. Dial settles down to a stable reading relatively quick. As a person needing 1.25 reader I found no issue with seeing the readings without the readers. Easy to read scale in the daylight while wearing polarized sunglasses. Luminescent "greenish" color allows for easy night sightings without killing your night vision. No batteries required:). Worst case situation would be a short exposure to a light source to recharge the luminous dial.

More or less floats on the surface of freshwater with no obvious moisture intrusion. Did not note any IPX rating on the packaging(long gone in the trash). Soft rubbery like housing allows for secure grip with bare wet hands or lightly gloved hands. Housing material should provide some protection from the eventual drop and the every day bumps. Neck lanyard and light weight should reduce drops and allow for all day wear. Housing should protect the unit from swing bumps.

Accuracy checked against an older Silvia Ranger type15 and Garmin GPSMaps 78sc. Prism (hand bearing sighting) view is in degrees only. 1* increments. Viewed from above you have the degrees in 30* numerical with 5* marks and the cardinal points.

Personal preference for "cheek" style vs. "arm" style of bearing compass. 5-year warranty from an established(+50 years), reputable company. Good real world history of reliablility and function.

text_fidelity_a:
Saris Bike Racks, Bones Car Trunk Bicycle Rack Carrier, Mounts 3 Bikes, Black The Saris Super Bones 3 is a really fantastic high end bike rack. I've been using racks by Allen for several years, and while they have their issues, I thought they were a good value. This Saris model costs 8x what my Allen rack did. The difference in price and quality is quite staggering. I can't tell you if it's worth $400, but you do get what you pay for.

The most striking difference is the stability of the Saris rack. It doesn't have lots of loose straps to fly around, and the design makes it stay solid at highway speeds. It's very easy to adjust to each trunk. I can load it up with 3 bikes and it feels secure, even at 80mph. I could not say the same for my Allen rack. The Saris is also well padded to prevent scratches to the car. It also keeps the bike pedals far away enough so they don't damage the car. With the Allen rack, my pedals totally scratched up the Civic's bumper.

The disadvantages of the Saris rack are:
- The much higher cost
- Does not fold flat for storage
- Fits less cars, such as hatchbacks

This is clearly for the serious biker, so would use it very frequently to justify the price. You know who you are.
text_fidelity_b: Saris Bike Racks, Bones Car Trunk Bicycle Rack Carrier, Mounts 3 Bikes, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Slumberjack Tough Cot (32 x 82 x 19-Inch) We have several 4WD truck camping trips coming up this Spring, Summer, and Fall. We wanted to move from inflatable mattresses to cots in our 10' x 8' Kelty Ridge 6 tent. We were looking for a durable, comfortable cot that set up easily, left plenty of room for storage below the bed, was at least 32" wide, and could easily support 250 lbs without feeling like it was always on the verge of collapse. We tried several cots that cost anywhere between $40 and $150. The more expensive cots were comfortable and fit our needs, but we were having a tough time justifying the price. We were starting to rethink the move to cots until we both laid on the Slumberjack Tough Cot, a cot rated to 350 lbs. We bought two immediately at a local sports warehouse because it fit all our parameters for a great price.

When we opened the boxes we realized there are no instructions with the cots. Still, it took us less than five minutes to figure out how the cot sets up, including proper installation of the end-cap support bars. Once we had the process figured out the second cot took less than a minute to set up. Breakdown and stowage back in the bag takes maybe three minutes.

The cot is solidly constructed with very little sway when set up. The bed material is tough. Yep, the cot is heavy, but hey, we're not backpacking. We picked up a 3"x32"x82" foam pad for $20 at a local hardware store, cover it with a sheet, throw down the sleeping bag, and crawl in for the night. Camping can often be an exercise in sleep deprivation due to the lack of comfort. NOT WITH THESE BABIES! My wife and I both LOVE sleeping on these cots with the foam pad mentioned. It feels downright decadent compared to the blowup mattresses we used to use. The Slumberjack Tough Cot was one of the best purchases ever for our camping fun.

We're looking forward to years of use from our Slumberjack Tough Cots.
text_fidelity_b: Slumberjack Tough Cot (32 x 82 x 19-Inch)

We’d been out for a few days, enjoying things, when we got caught out. We do go out with light rain ponchos, but they can get hot, sticky, and not cover very well. This last time was, well, the last time we wanted to use them. I had been looking for a rain jacket for both my wife and I and spotted this Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker for myself. I am already thrilled with it and I haven’t even worn it in the rain. This Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker looks great! I love the navy, the reflective line, and the layout of the pockets. I put it on and it was a perfect fit. The cut is good - I feel like I can wear just my t shirt or light color shirt and shorts and I’ll be covered well. But I’m also loosing weight, so I feel like as I do, it’ll get big, but still cover me well, perhaps even better.

There is great placement of velcro - at the wrists to hold it tight, along the front to keep it truly secure. The front zipper is covered so as to not let rain in the front. The hood comes up and over, with the ability to pull it down “tight” to protect the face/head. The material truly does feel like it’ll repel rain and keep me dry. I also have to think about keeping cool - in our hot, humid state rain can make things even more steamy - and this feels like it’ll be good. I’m not saying I’ll be “cool,” but rather comfortable in the rain.

I hope we have some rain in the coming days, as predicted, and as soon as we do, I’ll give it a good test. But until then, I’m already thrilled and happy to have this Freetrack Men's Reflective Cycling Rain Jacket Waterproof Hooded Windbreaker. Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain First off, these are by far the brightest reflective anything I've ever bought, and I've bought >20 wrist bands, arm bands, leg bands, vests, .... Photons apparently hate this material: every single photon that hits it immediately turns right around and heads back where it came from. You will be seen when you're wearing these. They're so bright you may be seen from space. :)

Second, customer service can't be beat. I ordered both the the wrist bands and the leg bands, but only received the wrist bands. I contacted the vendor, Mark, and he sent the leg bands out within 12 hours of receiving my email. Later I had a problem with the reflective material separating from the neoprene on one one of the wrist bands, and Mark didn't just replace the one that failed, he sent me a whole new pair, and very quickly. So this is a low-risk purchase: if you have any issues, Mark will make it right for you.

One thing I'm not fond of is that the hook portion of the hook and loop closure is too long. Unless the band fits perfectly around your leg, a good sized section of the hook portion will be exposed, and can snag on cyclists' lycra gear. I wish the hook portion was just an inch long. The 3" loop portion would still allow a couple of inches of flexibility re length.

Also, I'm not sure why these have both extra long hook and loop closures and are made of stretchy neoprene. Both seem intended to allow the band to fit different diameters of legs + clothing, so I'm not sure why you need both. And the stretchy neoprene makes it much more likely that the relatively delicate reflective material will separate from it, as happened with 1 of the 4 bands I originally purchased. I'd prefer the fabric to not stretch to minimize the risk of failure, and just use the velcro to adjust the length. But since Mark backs up the product if it fails, this is a small deal.

Overall, I'm happy with these. I believe they're the brightest reflective bands you can buy, so if you want to be seen, these will do the job.
text_fidelity_b: Leg Shield Reflective Ankle Bands - Very Large Reflective Area for Greater Visibility - Bright, Comfortable, Neoprene - Straps for Biking, Running, Walking - Protects Cyclist's Pants from Chain

LaserLyte NAA 22 Magnum Laser Sight I have been carrying a NAA .22 mag probably for 25 years now. In hot and muggy Southwest Florida, having a stainless steel mini revolver tucked in your pocket allows you to carry concealed without anyone knowing. It's light, holds five bullets, is easily controllable, won't rust when damp, and can be brought to play in seconds. NAA as a company stands by their weapons and have reconditioned mine twice for free. The biggest drawbacks to this gun (although no gun is perfect) are twofold. While a .22 magnum bullet is considerably more powerful that a .22 long rifle, the extremely short barrel of the NAA doesn't allow the bullet to reach the higher velocities that it is intended to provide. In addition, the sights on the gun don't allow for more than a "point and shoot" at short distances with any accuracy. Of course you could quibble about the size of the gun, the slippery grips, the lack of bullet capacity, and any other shortcoming that might affect your choice of weapon. My philosophy has always been that any gun when you need it is better than no gun at all.

The recent introduction of short barreled ammunition has helped punch up the power of the .22 magnum through the NAA guns. While everyone knows that being shot with a regular .22 LR can be deadly, having a short barrel .22 magnum round fired at you will arrive with a lot bigger punch. And then of course the sights on the NAA guns are relatively useless because of the very short barrel. Laserlyte came up with this nifty idea of putting a laser sight in a grip that replaces the standard grips on the NAA .22 magnum. When properly mounted and used, this extends the useful range on this tiny weapon enough to keep any assailants at a greater distance. The sight of a red dot on someone's chest can be a tremendous deterrent, even without knowing what gun it's mounted on and without a shot being fired. That should give an assailant pause and also allow you to tactfully retreat to a safer area.

The Laserlyte NAA .22 Mag Grip Laser comes well protected in a hard plastic package with three batteries already inserted in the grips, three extra batteries for your first replacement, an instruction manual showing how to remove the old grips and install the new ones, and three hex wrenches--a larger one to fasten the grips together and two smaller ones to adjust windage and elevation. Installing the new grips took a little extra effort on my part. The hard plastic that the grips are made of were slightly too large to fit smoothly against the frame and gently cranking down the fastener left some gaps in the fit. I ended up taking them apart and putting them together about four times before they finally slipped into the proper alignment with no gaps remaining. There are a couple of things that LaserLyte could do to upgrade the grips. It would of course help if they were machined to a slightly looser tolerance. Putting some kind of texture on the grips would be helpful by making them less slippery. Alternatively, using a softer molded plastic would give a better fit and grip at the same time.

I haven't had time to go to the range to adjust the windage and elevation yet. When I do, I'll be sure to follow another reviewer's suggestion to "gently" use the hex tool on the tiny screws provided in the grip. We're talking really tiny here and it appears that it wouldn't take much pressure to strip the screws and render them useless. If that works out for me and brings the sights on target, I will be a pretty satisfied buyer. But the hard plastic construction of this product is a recipe for disaster. There is nothing robust about this design and it probably wouldn't take much to crack the grips or break off the small laser housing. This is a good start by LaserLyte but they have to come up with several improvements to make their product more durable. An oversize grip wouldn't be asking too much, would it?

NOTE: If you pocket carry this little gun with the mounted laser, you can no longer carry it without a holster. Carrying it without the holster allows the gun to jostle and throws off the laser sights. Not good! Please be advised that mounting this laser on your NAA .22 mag will not allow it to fit in many holsters intended for this firearm.
text_fidelity_b: LaserLyte NAA 22 Magnum Laser Sight

Wipkal 2 Pcs New Cooling Hat Ice Hat Wide Brim Cap, Summer Sun Hat Sunscreen Cooling Air Conditioning Cap Ice Cap Towel UV Protection for Women Men Light Gray Thought this will beat the traditional hay hats, wrong!
Hat is way too large in diameter. You will catch yourself bumping into everything. Sort of like wearing two numbers larger shoes, try it! it's annoying and so is the round hat, I guarantee you.
Next non-sense with the round hat is the side slits behind the mesh let the sun in. Rating sun protection 1 star as it defies the purpose of why I ended up buying this in first place; and If I posted picturet after first couple hours of wearing it outside in decent yet not extreme heat, you'd be horrified to notice the staining from sweat after it dries, in repeated sessions. It looks disgusting. Fabric, or faux leather, whatever the outer coating is made of, does not give an indication of long lasting life of a product, instead I expect it to peel soon, matter of fact, mesh on one side is already ripping off a good section at the lower seam due to not so precise stitching that skipped the mesh thanks to its large openings. The central insulation material that seem to be the same glossy flex aluminum you see inside the small refrigeration lunch bags is incredibly thin and expected to rip after a year or two of use - IF nothing else rips before it of course. (mesh pun intended)
Finally the inner blue "cooling" fabric that is to be wetted... impressions after handling it is nothing like what one thinks of when ordering this set. Thought it'll be pretty thick to absorb enough liquid to provide lasting cooling effect. What you will get? Another thin layer, to me these words immediately jumped into my mind: "A blue toilet paper, or is it actual fabric?" Yep, those are the impressions and the rating solely for the round hat so far.
I have yet to try the baseball type hat, but I dont see it to be any better except I wont be bumping my head against the firm hat that loves to bump into everything around you. On the other hand, sun protection is limited with baseball type hat as it doesnt cover in entire circle but a small section. Like I said in the headline, I dont know.
To me it seems that its rather a gimmick, poorly executed at that.
Not that it couldnt be a good product, if it was manufactured with PRO skilled team that would research, test and fix issues that I'm finding out on my own stupidity for wasting money on it even!
Only 5 stars are for the light weight but guess if I still wear it? After about a week? 10 hours of use I'm back to good old school hay hat I got good few years back and cant be happier!
Hope this reading helps you decide, better stuff your old hay hat with wet toilet paper and you'll be better with it than with this nonsensical pile of garbage that should never been manufactured as all it may do is pollute Earth with more artificial toxic materials causing all sorts of skin issues on humans, animals and foliage.
